title: CVS agrees to pay $315 million to settle case over opioid prescriptions
summary: CVS Pharmacy Inc. and various subsidiaries have agreed to pay $315 million to resolve a Justice Department case alleging it unlawfully dispensed medically unnecessary prescriptions of highly addictive opioids
story: CVS Pharmacy Inc. and various subsidiaries have agreed to pay $315 million to resolve a Justice Department case alleging it unlawfully dispensed medically unnecessary prescriptions of highly addictive opioids

WASHINGTON -- CVS Pharmacy Inc. and various subsidiaries have agreed to pay $315 million to resolve a Justice Department case alleging it unlawfully dispensed medically unnecessary prescriptions of highly addictive opioids, officials said Tuesday.

The settlement resolves a lawsuit brought in 2024 that accused the healthcare giant of prescribing massive amounts of opioids and other controlled substances “to fuel its own profits at the expense of public health and safety.”
It’s the latest effort by the federal government to hold accountable companies that officials have alleged helped fuel the U.S. addiction and overdose crisis.

“Today’s settlement is a significant milestone in the Justice Department’s efforts to combat the opioid epidemic by cracking down on pharmacies who unlawfully fulfill prescriptions for controlled substances," Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward said in an emailed statement.

CVS said in a statement that its pharmacists were trained “in the safe and appropriate use of all medications” and that it had implemented “best-in-class” programs to help them “make the best decisions on behalf of patients.”
The company said it strongly disagreed with the claims made in the lawsuit and that the settlement admits no wrongdoing.
The company said in 2024 that pharmacists were being held to “vague, undefined, and ever-changing standards of practice” when it comes to filling prescription opioids.

The lawsuit filed under President Joe Biden's administration accused CVS of violating the Controlled Substances Act by filling illegitimate prescriptions for high doses of potent opioids that “fed dependence and addiction.” The Justice Department alleged it dispensed large quantities of opioids based on prescriptions from known “pill mills," or providers that hand out prescriptions for drugs without a legitimate medical purpose.

It alleged that poor staffing levels coupled with performance metrics and incentive compensation policies implemented by the company led to pharmacists racing to fill prescriptions without confirming they were legitimate. The prescriptions were often billed to and reimbursed by Medicaid and other federal healthcare programs, the lawsuit says.

Under the settlement, CVS must also "implement additional safeguards to ensure that prescriptions for opioids and other controlled substances are dispensed only when medically appropriate,” Assistant Attorney General Brett Shumate, who leads the Justice Department’s Civil Division, said in a statement.

Over the last decade, drugmakers, wholesalers, pharmacies and other companies have agreed to settlements with governments in the U.S. totaling over $50 billion. Most of the money is intended to go to address the crisis, which has been linked to more than 100,000 deaths in the U.S. some years, though the numbers have fallen sharply recently.

Most of the settlements -- and dollars -- have been with state and local governments, but the U.S. has reached several deals, including in the last two years with the pharmacies Walgreens and Walmart.
Associated Press reporter Geoff Mulvihill contributed to this report from Philadelphia.

title: Cyberattack targeting refrigeration systems hits 700 supermarkets
summary: Cyberattacks have disrupted European supermarket chains, causing refrigeration systems to overheat at hundreds of stores in France
story: Cyberattacks have disrupted European supermarket chains, causing refrigeration systems to overheat at hundreds of stores in France

PARIS -- Cyberattacks have disrupted European supermarket chains, causing refrigeration systems to overheat at hundreds of stores in France and forcing a major grocer to shut down websites serving customers in Europe and the United States.

French Finance Minister Roland Lescure told Parliament on Tuesday that about 700 of the country’s 10,000 supermarkets were affected. He said there was no risk to France’s food supplies but acknowledged that the attack “touches the heart of our food security.”
″It was a wake-up call for everyone,” he said.
The Paris prosecutor’s office said Tuesday that its cybercrime unit was investigating the large-scale attack, including the extent of damage caused by spoiled food and possible fires.

Dominique Schelcher, CEO of French grocery chain Cooperative U, said 80 of the company’s 2,000 stores were affected. Most managed to prevent disruptions to refrigeration, but some had to discard food, he said in a post on X.
“Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products is an attack on the French food supply chain. It is unprecedented, extremely serious, and unacceptable,” Schelcher said.

Danish technology company Danfoss, which supplied the refrigeration management software, said Monday that most affected systems were older products that no longer received software or security updates.
“Danfoss has long advised customers to keep supported systems updated with the latest firmware, as well as to operate behind a firewall,” the company said.
Danfoss said it was working with affected customers to limit the damage.

Separately, Dutch supermarket giant Ahold Delhaize said Tuesday it was working to restore systems it had shut down following what it described as a security issue. The company, which operates Albert Heijn in the Netherlands, Delhaize in Belgium and Stop & Shop in the United States, declined to provide further details.
Websites for several of its brands, including Stop & Shop, Food Lion and Albert Heijn, remained offline Tuesday, although stores were open and serving customers.
Ahold Delhaize said it had no evidence that customer or employee data had been stolen.

“Protecting our infrastructure in the best interest of our customers, associates and partners is a top priority,” the company said. “We apologize for any inconvenience this issue may have caused customers and partners.”

title: Kroger to lay off 3K corporate employees over 3 years as it leans into AI
summary: Grocery store chain Kroger says it will lay off 3,000 corporate employees over the next three years as it ramps up its use of artificial intelligence to streamline operations
story: Grocery store chain Kroger says it will lay off 3,000 corporate employees over the next three years as it ramps up its use of artificial intelligence to streamline operations
Grocery store chain Kroger said it will lay off 3,000 corporate employees over the next three years as it ramps up its use of artificial intelligence to streamline operations.

“Technology is reshaping what’s possible,” CEO Greg Foran wrote in a memo to employees on Monday. “The way work gets done is changing across every industry; we must adapt and take advantage of technology. We need to adopt capabilities, reduce duplicative work and look closely at where work is best fit to be done.”
Kroger last month outlined its AI strategy, meant “to improve the customer experience, make work easier for associates and produce better business outcomes.”

Cincinnati-based Kroger is the largest standalone U.S. supermarket chain with 409,000 employees and more than 2,700 stores operating under various brands, including Ralphs, King Soopers, Smith’s and Fred Meyer.
Kroger named former Walmart executive Foran CEO in February, 11 months after the abrupt resignation of its previous CEO.

Foran has a reputation for being tech-savvy and detail-oriented. He led Walmart’s U.S. division from 2014 to 2019, where he focused on cleaning up stores, ensuring items were in stock and improving the fresh produce selection. He also introduced online ordering and pickup, and accelerated Walmart’s digital capabilities.
Walmart has become a larger challenge to Kroger and other traditional grocers as Americans increasingly pick up their groceries along with other general goods that Walmart sells.
Kroger has also felt pressure from fast-growing discount chains like Aldi and Lidl and online behemoths like Amazon.

Kroger proposed a merger with Albertsons in 2022 as a way to better compete with its rivals. But the Federal Trade Commission and two states — Washington and Colorado — sued to block the merger in 2024, saying it would raise prices and lower workers’ wages by eliminating competition. Judges ultimately ruled that the merger should not proceed.
A day after their merger collapsed, Albertsons filed a lawsuit against Kroger, seeking a $600 million termination fee as well as billions of dollars in legal fees and lost shareholder value.
Kroger said the claims were “baseless” and that Albertsons was not entitled to the fee.
Kroger shares fell 1.6% in morning trading Tuesday, to $61.66.

title: UK's Burnham weighs approval for oil and gas drilling in the North Sea
summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham faces a crucial decision on whether to allow oil and gas drilling in the North Sea
story: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham faces a crucial decision on whether to allow oil and gas drilling in the North Sea
LONDON -- British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is facing a key test of his environmental policies as he decides on whether oil and gas companies should be allowed to drill in the North Sea.

Burnham's government has been under heavy pressure from climate campaigners and businesses over whether to approve two oil and gas fields in waters north of Scotland, including one said to be the U.K.'s largest untapped oil resource.

Environmental groups have urged Burnham to refuse permission for the projects, known as Rosebank and Jackdaw, saying they would accelerate climate change at a time when the U.K., like the rest of Europe, faces record extreme heat linked to human actions including burning fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas.

But opposition politicians, the oil and gas industry and U.S. President Donald Trump have piled pressure on Burnham to give the green light, arguing it would protect jobs, cut household bills and boost Britain’s energy security.
British officials have been expected to make a decision since August, when public consultations on the two projects closed.

Rosebank is an oil field that also will produce gas. Located 80 miles (130 kilometers) north of Scotland's Shetland Islands, it is estimated to be the largest undeveloped oil and gas field in the U.K., reportedly with capacity to produce 300 million to 500 million barrels of oil within about 25 years.

Jackdaw is a gas field 150 miles east of Aberdeen on Scotland's northeast coast. Production there was expected to last under a decade. The Shell Group, one of the project's co-developers, predicts the field can produce around 6.5% of the U.K.’s gas production at its peak.
The opposition Conservative Party, which has pushed for the developments to go ahead, said the Jackdaw field could start heating 1.4 million homes in the U.K. this winter if approved.

The former Conservative government previously approved production at both sites, which were scheduled to start operations later this year. But a court in Edinburgh ruled last year that the approvals were unlawful, after considering a legal challenge from Greenpeace and another nonprofit.

“The public interest in authorities acting lawfully and the private interest of members of the public in climate change outweigh the private interest of the developers,” judge Andrew Stewart ruled at the time.

Critics have argued that the oil and gas reserves in Britain's North Sea holdings are small and would make little difference to energy bills because prices are decided by international markets. They contend that new developments would increase carbon emissions while failing to contribute to Britain's energy security.
Analysts at the Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit, a London-based nonprofit, estimated that more than 90% of the oil and gas likely to be produced from the North Sea has already been extracted.

“We’ve just had record-breaking heat waves this summer, wildfires, half of the country’s still in drought. We’re facing potential crop failures and food shortages this winter from a super El Niño,” said Victoria Smith, a Fossil Free London activist protesting on Tuesday.
“Drilling for new oil and gas now ... would just be a wild decision, completely reckless by this government," she said.
Almost 600 climate and health experts wrote a joint letter to the government last month arguing that approving the projects would breach the U.K.'s national and international climate commitments.

Separately, critics also have raised concerns about Rosebank's links to Israeli company Delek Group, which activists say profited from Israeli settlements in the West Bank. Green Party leader Zach Polanski is among critics who have asked how the U.K. can ensure revenue from any oil and gas production did not finance the settlements.

Supporters of further drilling say it will not make a significant difference to emissions and is vital for protecting jobs. Some also argue that domestic production will result in less carbon emissions than importing oil and gas.

The governing Labour Party is split on the issue. Some warned that going ahead will renege on the party's pledge in its 2024 manifesto not to issue new licenses for oil and gas exploration in the North Sea.
Others disagree. “If we do not proceed with Jackdaw and Rosebank, investment will leave the UK, jobs will disappear and expertise will be lost,” lawmaker Graeme Downie said.

The issue became more politicized after Trump waded in. The U.S. president, who criticized former Prime Minister Keir Starmer's energy policies, claimed in August that people in Aberdeen were “dancing in the streets” following reports that Burnham would approve new drilling.
In his first phone call with Trump, Burnham reportedly said the U.K. “can’t ignore” resources in the North Sea, adding he would take “a pragmatic approach” to further drilling.
Britain's government has declined to directly comment, only saying the North Sea “remains a vital national asset.”

“Any decision will take into account all relevant evidence, including environmental assessments and public representations received as part of the regulatory process,” the energy security department said.
AP journalist Kwiyeon Ha contributed.

title: US home sales rose in September, but slowed from a year earlier
summary: Sales of previously occupied U.S. homes rose in September from the previous month, but slowed compared to a year ago, the latest sign the housing market remains stalled as rising mortgage rates and home prices discourage prospective homebuyers
story: Sales of previously occupied U.S. homes rose in September from the previous month, but slowed compared to a year ago, the latest sign the housing market remains stalled as rising mortgage rates and home prices discourage prospective homebuyers

Sales of previously occupied U.S. homes rose in September from the previous month, but slowed compared to a year ago, the latest sign the housing market remains stalled as rising mortgage rates and home prices discourage prospective homebuyers.

Existing home sales rose 1.5% last month from August to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.99 million units, the National Association of Realtors said Tuesday. One of the factors in the monthly increase is that sales in August were revised lower.
Sales fell 2.2% compared with September last year. The latest sales tally is slightly above the 3.98 million pace economists were expecting, according to FactSet.

Home sales have been mostly hovering close to a 4-million annual pace going back to 2023, far short of the historic norm that is closer to 5.2-million. September is the second month in a row that the annual sales pace has remained below 4 million.

Home prices continued to rise nationally last month. The U.S. median sales price increased 1.3% in September from a year earlier to $417,500, an all-time high for the month of September based on data going back to 1999, NAR said. Home prices have risen on an annual basis for 39 months in a row.
“This is a very tough market out there, especially with mortgage rates rising,” said Lawrence Yun, NAR’s chief economist.

The U.S. housing market has been in a slump since 2022, when mortgage rates began to climb from pandemic-era lows. Sales of previously occupied U.S. homes were essentially flat last year, stuck at a 30-year low.

This year, sales have been in a rut in large part due to rising borrowing costs, as mortgage rates have marched higher in the months since the war between the U.S. and Iran started in late February. Expectations of higher inflation amid surging oil prices have pushed up the long-term bond yields that lenders use as a guide to pricing home loans, driving mortgage rates higher.
The average rate on the benchmark 30-year mortgage hit 7.4% last week, its highest level in nearly three years. It briefly dipped below 6% before the war started.
Many of the homes purchased last month likely went under contract in August and July, when the average rate on a 30-year mortgage ranged from 6.43% to 6.69%, according to Freddie Mac.

Mortgage rates are not likely to drop meaningfully any time soon, given the ongoing uncertainty over oil prices, geopolitical tensions, the exploding U.S. government debt and other factors that have been driving rates on home loans higher, Yun said.
Homebuyers should consider mortgage rates at 7%, or slightly above 7%, “the new normal,” he said.
The sharp rise in mortgage rates, which can add hundreds of dollars a month in costs for borrowers, has led many would-be home shoppers to put their home shopping plans on hold.
However, those who can afford to buy at current rates, or pay all cash, have a much wider selection of homes to choose from than they've had in years as properties sit on the market longer.

Although home inventory levels remain below historical norms, there were 1.6 million unsold homes at the end of last month — the highest level of unsold inventory on the market since November 2019, NAR said.
All told, unsold home inventory rose 1.9% last month from August and climbed 4.6% from September last year, NAR said.
September’s month-end inventory translates to a 4.8-months’ supply at the current sales pace. Traditionally, a 4- to 6-month supply is considered a balanced market between buyers and sellers.
The more balanced market gives home shoppers potentially more leverage in negotiating better terms with sellers, especially if a property has not fetched offers in weeks or months.
Consider, in September, the national median home listing price fell 1.2% from a year earlier to $419,250 as about 21% of listings had their initial price lowered, according to Realtor.com.
“The market is clearly tilting in favor of buyers able to negotiate for better prices,” Yun said.

title: Saudi Ministry of Energy reports limited fire in building at Aramco compound targeted in attack
summary: The Saudi Ministry of Energy says a limited fire broke out in an administrative building in Aramco, one of the world’s largest oil facilities, that was targeted in the country's Eastern Province
story: The Saudi Ministry of Energy says a limited fire broke out in an administrative building in Aramco, one of the world’s largest oil facilities, that was targeted in the country's Eastern Province

CAIRO -- A limited fire broke out Tuesday in an administrative building at Aramco, one of the world’s largest oil facilities, that was targeted in an attack in the country’s Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy said. The ministry said no injuries were reported.

The attack came as the Iranian-backed Houthis and the Saudi coalition fighting them exchanged attacks Tuesday night. The fighting marked a fresh escalation in the widening Middle East crisis and came shortly after the Saudi coalition reported a series of alerts for incoming missiles heading for the Eastern Province, a major oil-producing region, and the capital Riyadh.
Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defense said debris from two intercepted Houthi missiles fell on residential areas in Riyadh, injuring four people and damaging 15 homes.
The coalition of forces in Yemen led by Saudi Arabia carried out new airstrikes Tuesday on the Houthi rebel-held Yemeni capital, the Houthi-run broadcaster Al Masirah and residents said.

The strikes came shortly after a coalition spokesman urged residents to evacuate the area for their safety. Witnesses reported hearing strong explosions in Sanaa hours after the coalition struck the Subaha fuel facility west of the city.

In a rare statement earlier, the coalition had urged civilians in the Houthi-controlled capital to leave the Yemeni Oil Company site, on a hill overlooking the capital, and nearby storage areas ahead of a possible strike.
Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki accused the Houthis of using the facility and its underground fuel depots for their arsenal of missiles and drones.

Houthi officials appeared to have anticipated the attack. The oil company said its storage facilities were empty and that a Saudi strike would not affect oil reserves or supplies for residents. Still, witnesses in the city said lines of cars formed at some gas stations amid fears of a shortage.

Shortly after the warning, Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said on Telegram that any Saudi attack on Sanaa would be met with a “firm and painful” response in the Saudi capital, Riyadh.

Hours later, Saudi Arabia issued alerts for incoming missiles heading for Riyadh and the Eastern Province but quickly said the danger had passed. The coalition said it had intercepted a series of Houthi-launched ballistic missiles, drones and cruise missiles in multiple areas in the country, including Riyadh and the southern province of Wadi al-Dawasir. Riyadh residents reported hearing loud explosions.

Airlines moved a number of their planes out of Riyadh on Tuesday on the advice of insurers and government officials because of the threat of additional attacks. They needed to transfer the planes to other airports in the country so they can keep flying passengers to their destinations, said Osprey Flight Solutions Chief Intelligence Officer Matthew Borie, whose company advises airlines, insurers and countries on flight threats.
“It’s not abnormal for this to occur especially in this day and age with the types of conflict zone situations that have occurred in the region,” Borie said.

More than 3,120 flights scheduled to depart from airports across Saudi Arabia since Oct. 8 have been canceled or listed as not operating, representing about 41% of scheduled departures, according to aviation analytics firm Cirium. That includes more than 300 flights that had been scheduled to depart Wednesday.
Several airlines have suspended service to the kingdom because of the Houthi attacks on airports.
It was unclear whether the Tuesday strike in Yemen was a signal of military escalation or a carefully measured response to recent deadly attacks on the Riyadh airport.

The warning and the attack show “the Saudis’ aims of upping the ante and striking deep in the heart of Houthi-controlled territory while attempting to control the narrative by presenting themselves as more careful and humanitarian actors than the Houthis,” said Adam Baron, a fellow at the Washington-based New America institute.
“It may be a warning — or it may be a sign of things to come," he said.

Saudi Arabia is still scrambling to determine how its air defenses failed to intercept a barrage of missiles and drones fired by the Houthis, including an attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday that killed at least 13 people and wounded over 300.

The latest conflict between the Saudis and the Houthis began last month after the rebels seized key areas along the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical waterway for the transport of Gulf oil and other goods at the southern end of the Red Sea off Yemen.
The Saudi-led coalition, backing forces aligned with Yemen’s internationally recognized government, has been trying to retake them.
Saudi Arabia’s Cabinet on Tuesday warned the Houthis they would “face consequences” for their repeated attacks on the kingdom.

“The Kingdom will not allow any threat to its security or to freedom of maritime navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait,” the Cabinet said in a statement carried by Saudi state-owned Al-Ekhbariya television. The Bab el-Mandeb is another area key to the flow of oil out of the Persian Gulf.

On Tuesday, Yemen’s interior ministry said in a statement on X that Houthi strikes over the past day on Taiz, a major city in the country's southwest, had killed six people and injured 18 amid ongoing battles in the region.

A commander with the Saudi-backed forces said rebels had fought through fierce resistance to reach the edges of Taiz, and some had entered the city. The fight was now critical for Taiz, which has long been a sought-after prize, he said.
The commander, speaking on condition of anonymity to describe battlefield details, said rebel forces were surprisingly large, and bolstered by medium and short-range ballistic missiles.

That fighting is leading to the large-scale displacement of people and growing shortages of food and other supplies, U.N. spokesman Stephane Dujarric said Tuesday, with cooking gas largely unavailable and food prices that have reportedly risen about 50%.
Saudi Arabia has been pushing for the U.S. military to provide more direct support in the fight against the Houthis.
The U.S. has provided intelligence sharing, target identification and planning for a Saudi-led offensive, but has held off on carrying out strikes against the Houthis.
A U.S. intervention could prompt the Houthis to try to halt shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb.
Associated Press writers Sarah El Deeb in Beirut, Samy Magdy in Cairo, Aamer Madhani in Jerusalem, Rio Yamat in Las Vegas, and AP Transportation Writer Josh Funk in Omaha, Nebraska, contributed.

title: What to know about the Nord Stream pipeline explosions trial opening in Germany this week
summary: A former Ukrainian army officer is going on trial in Germany over undersea explosions that damaged the Nord Stream gas pipelines between Russia and Germany four years ago
story: A former Ukrainian army officer is going on trial in Germany over undersea explosions that damaged the Nord Stream gas pipelines between Russia and Germany four years ago

BERLIN -- A former Ukrainian army officer is going on trial in Germany this week over undersea explosions that damaged the Nord Stream gas pipelines between Russia and Germany four years ago in one of the biggest acts of sabotage in Europe since the Second World War.
The suspect faces charges of causing an explosion, damaging property, disrupting public service and being an “accomplice to war crimes” by attacking civilian infrastructure, according to prosecutors.
The attack laid bare Europe's dependence on Russian energy but also raised sensitive questions about Ukraine and its Western allies.

While international observers initially blamed Moscow, there are now increasing suggestions that Ukrainian state security agencies may have been involved — even though Ukraine counts Germany as one of its closest allies.
According to German privacy rules, the suspect will be identified in court only as Serhii K., although he was publicly named as Serhii Kuznietsov in extradition proceedings in Italy.

Here's what we know about the alleged ringleader of the attack and one of the most politically charged court cases of wartime sabotage that will be heard at the Hanseatic Higher Regional Court in Hamburg starting this Wednesday.
The explosions on Sept. 26, 2022, damaged pipelines that were built to carry Russian natural gas to Germany under the Baltic Sea.
At the time, European countries were moving to wean themselves off Russian energy sources, following the Kremlin’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Prosecutors say the aim of the plot was to permanently disrupt gas deliveries and prevent Russia from using the revenues to finance its military operations.
The defendant and others allegedly used a yacht that set off from the German port of Rostock. It had been hired from a German company using forged IDs and with the help of intermediaries.

The explosions ruptured the Nord Stream 1 pipeline, which was Russia’s main natural gas supply route to Germany until Moscow cut off supplies in August 2022. They also damaged Nord Stream 2, which never entered service because Germany suspended its certification process shortly before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

The suspect allegedly organized and carried out the detonation of at least four bombs between 14 and 27 kilograms (around 31 to 62 pounds) at a depth of 70 to 80 meters (230 feet to 263 feet) near the Danish island of Bornholm.

He was detained in August in an Italian village, where officers raided a bungalow where he was staying with his family. Police said he surrendered without resistance. He was extradited to Germany in November.
A second suspect was arrested on a European warrant in the northern Croatian town of Pula in August. He has applied for asylum in Croatia to fight his extradition to Germany.
The pipelines were long a target of criticism by the U.S. and some of its allies, which warned that they increased dependence on Russian gas.

Russian officials, however, have claimed that U.S. and British intelligence agencies were involved in staging the explosions, which Moscow declared “an act of international terrorism,” and have launched their own investigation.
Russia has also accused NATO of involvement in the attack, while several Western countries initially blamed Russia.
More recently, the Kremlin has expressed hope that those who orchestrated the explosions will be held accountable.
Asked what Moscow expects from the trial, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Monday that “we expect objectivity.”
“We expect … that both the perpetrators and those who ordered it will be named. That would be very important. I think no one doubts who it really is,” Peskov said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has denied allegations that his country was involved in the pipeline blasts.

He also told reporters in August that Ukraine’s prosecutors and Foreign Ministry were already cooperating with partners and that Kyiv was “absolutely open to joint steps on the investigation,” stressing the importance of keeping Europe’s trust.

Nonetheless, “all the evidence points very clearly to the fact that Ukraine blew up the Nord Stream pipelines, not the Russians, whom they initially tried to pin the blame on,” says Joachim Weber, a security expert at the Center for Advanced Security, Strategic and Integration Studies at the University of Bonn.

“This is, of course, highly explosive politically, because, as is well known, Germany is one of Ukraine’s closest allies, supporting the country on a massive scale with huge sums of money and also by taking on considerable political risks,” Weber said.
However, the German government has so far refrained from comment on the upcoming trial, pointing out that no verdict has yet been reached and the case is in the hands of the independent judiciary.

Even if it were proven in the course of the trial that Ukrainian government agencies were somehow involved in the sabotage act, that would likely have few consequences for Germany’s relationship with Ukraine, “because we naturally want Ukraine to survive,” not least as a buffer against Russia, said Weber.
“In that respect — even if it sounds cynical to some — Ukraine also serves a purpose for us, and it is in our interest to preserve it,” he said.
The outcome of the trial is unlikely to have major repercussions on German-Ukrainian relations, he argued.
“In short, I don’t see us going through some kind of list of punishments against Ukraine right now,” Weber said. “But we should take this as a warning, so to speak, to view things realistically.”
Niemann reported from Bonn, Germany. AP writers Hanna Arhirova in Kyiv, Ukraine and Jovana Gec in Belgrade, Serbia contributed reporting.

title: Longhorns and Gators clash with bruised bodies and egos needing win to keep their seasons on track
summary: Three weeks ago, the Texas-Florida matchup looked like a potential blockbuster
story: Three weeks ago, the Texas-Florida matchup looked like a potential blockbuster
AUSTIN, Texas -- Three weeks ago, the Texas-Florida matchup looked like a blockbuster.
The Longhorns were No. 1 behind quarterback Arch Manning. The Gators were storming up the rankings behind first-year coach Jon Sumrall and igniting the chomp in the Swamp.
Those were good times. Both teams now limp into Saturday's game in Austin with bruised bodies and egos, and carrying a whiff of desperation for a win to keep the season from unraveling.

Seventh-ranked Texas (4-1, 1-1 SEC) is back home after a deflating loss to unranked archrival Oklahoma in Dallas, where Manning threw a pair of costly fourth-quarter interceptions. The Gators (4-2, 2-2) are probably glad to hit the road after a getting run out of the Swamp last week by South Carolina.
Texas was shaken by the loss, but is still in the hunt for the SEC championship and the College Football Playoff.
Manning said this week he's looking forward to a rematch with the Gators, who handed Texas a humbling defeat last year. That loss that played a big role in the Longhorns' not reaching the playoff.
“Obviously a new (Florida) coach and they have some new players, but it left a bad taste in my mouth,” Manning said.

The Gators looked great when they blasted Ole Miss last month. But those home cheers turned into some boos in last week's 38-19 loss to South Carolina. The defeat exposed just how far a program with talented players still has to go.
“We’re a work in progress," Sumrall said. "Sometimes our progress is dysfunctional.”

Florida starting quarterback Aaron Philo was listed as questionable Thursday because of a shoulder injury that limited his practice time. If he doesn't play, sophomore Trammel Jones would make his first career start. The Gators are hopeful they will have star receiver Vernell Brown III after missing the last two games with a knee injury.

The Gators sacked Manning six times last season and pass protection was a problem for Texas all year. Manning says his protection is much improved, but he's still been sacked eight times the last two games. Manning blames himself for some of that.
“I haven't helped them out, getting the ball out (quicker)," he said. "I've been taking some unnecessary sacks.”

Texas special teams have been a huge problem of late. In the last two weeks, Texas gave up its first punt return touchdown since 2013 and its first punt block for a TD since 2009. Sarkisian has said he won't take special teams coaching duties away from assistant Jeff Banks.

The Longhorns aren't scaring anyone on offense and Sarkisian has come under fire for his play calling. Texas ranks 12th in the SEC in total offense at 379 yards per game. But the Gators' defensive struggles have been even worse. Florida ranks last in the SEC in total defense and had more than 20 missed tackles last week against South Carolina.
(Corrects spelling of Jon Sumrall's first name in original version)

title: Marcus Reus has goal, assist to back JT Marcinkowski as Galaxy blank Timbers 2-0
summary: Marco Reus had a goal and an assist to back JT Marcinkowski and the Los Angeles Galaxy beat the Portland Timbers 2-0
story: Marco Reus had a goal and an assist to back JT Marcinkowski and the Los Angeles Galaxy beat the Portland Timbers 2-0
CARSON, Calif. -- Marco Reus had a goal and an assist to back JT Marcinkowski and the Los Angeles Galaxy beat the Portland Timbers 2-0 on Wednesday night.
Reus staked the Galaxy (10-11-9) to a 1-0 lead in the 17th minute when he used assists from Robert Taylor and Pablo Ruiz to score his eighth goal of the campaign.
That's where the score stood until Reus set up up Justin Haak in the 80th minute for his second goal this season and his fourth in 110 career matches. It was the career-high 11th assist for Reus.
Marcinkowski finished with five saves for Los Angeles. It was his fourth clean sheet in 24 starts this season.
James Pantemis stopped three shots for Portland (9-14-6).
The two clubs played to a 1-1 draw in Portland to close out March.
The Galaxy improve to 6-4-5 at home, while the Timbers fall to 2-10-3 on the road.
Portland has gone 1-4-2 since the start of September.
Portland: Hosts Colorado Rapids on Saturday.
Los Angeles: Hosts San Diego FC on Saturday.

title: Pirani, Dreyer and Bakambu score goals for San Diego in 3-3 tie with Dynamo
summary: Gabriel Pirani scored in the 86th minute for San Diego FC in a 3-3 tie with the Houston Dynamo
story: Gabriel Pirani scored in the 86th minute for San Diego FC in a 3-3 tie with the Houston Dynamo
SAN DIEGO -- Gabriel Pirani scored in the 86th minute for San Diego FC in a 3-3 tie with the Houston Dynamo on Wednesday night.
Anders Dreyer and Cédric Bakambu each added a goal for San Diego (8-12-9), which is winless in seven straight.
Guilherme had two goals and an assists for Houston and Mateusz Bogusz added a goal and an assist.
Manu Duah flicked a back-heel shot that bounced off the post and Pirani tapped the putback into a wide-open net.
The Dynamo (13-9-7) is winless in five straight.

Dreyer converted from the penalty spot to open the scoring in the 20th minute. Bakambu’s first-touch finish, off a feed from Onni Valakari, from the top of the 18-yard box skipped off the bottom of the crossbar into the net and made it 2-0 in the 22nd.
Guilherme scored on the counter-attack in the 24th minute and his strike from 25 yards out in the 37th gave the Dynamo a 3-2 lead.
The 31-year-old Santos — known simply as “Guilherme” — has 16 goals and nine assists in 28 appearances this season, his first in MLS.
San Diego had 61% possession and outshot the Dynamo 18-10, 6-3 on target.
Jonathan Bond had three saves for Houston.

Bogusz made it 2-2 in the 33rd, his sixth goal contribution (three goals, three assists) in the last six games. Guilherme chipped an arcing entry pass to Bogusz, who played a first-touch header and then slipped a bicycle kick from near the penalty spot inside the right post.
Houston: Hosts Dallas on Saturday.
San Diego: Plays Saturday at the LA Galaxy.

title: Yeboah scores 16th goal this season for Minnesota in 2-2 tie with Rapids
summary: Kelvin Yeboah scored his career-high 16th goal this season Wednesday night for Minnesota United in a 2-2 tie with the Colorado Rapids
story: Kelvin Yeboah scored his career-high 16th goal this season Wednesday night for Minnesota United in a 2-2 tie with the Colorado Rapids
COMMERCE CITY, Colo. -- Kelvin Yeboah scored his career-high 16th goal this season Wednesday night for Minnesota United in a 2-2 tie with the Colorado Rapids.
Sayed Abu Farki subbed on for Keegan Rosenberry in the 60th minute, was shown a straight red card in the 68th and Colorado played a man down the rest of the way.

An own goal by Colorado’s Loïc Williams capped the scoring in the 83rd. Hansen left his line and Yeboah played a low ball in front of the net where Williams misplayed a left-foot clearance that, as he fell to the ground, bounced up and deflected off his left thigh into the net.

Yeboah stole a pass in the attacking third, raced to the center of the area and beat goalkeeper Nico Hansen with a rolling shot in the 52nd minute that made it 1-1. The 26-year-old has at least one goal contribution in nine consecutive games and has eight goals and three assists in that span.

Darren Yapi redirected a volley, off an arcing cross played into the area by Rosenberry, into the net to open the scoring in first-half stoppage time and Georgi Minoungou scored from point-blank range into a wide-open net to give the Rapids (11-13-5) a 2-1 lead in the 74th minute.
Minnesota (7-12-10) is winless, with five losses, in its last eight games.
Minnesota: Hosts St. Louis on Saturday.
Colorado: Plays Saturday at Portland.

title: Jack Jasinski scores in stoppage time as Earthquakes tie Real Salt Lake 1-1 to up unbeaten run to 8
summary: Defender Jack Jasinski subbed in and scored during second-half stoppage time after Real Salt Lake took a late lead, and the San Jose Earthquakes rallied for a 1-1 draw to extend their unbeaten streak to eight
story: Defender Jack Jasinski subbed in and scored during second-half stoppage time after Real Salt Lake took a late lead, and the San Jose Earthquakes rallied for a 1-1 draw to extend their unbeaten streak to eight

SANDY, Utah -- Defender Jack Jasinski subbed in and scored during second-half stoppage time after Real Salt Lake took a late lead, and the San Jose Earthquakes rallied for a 1-1 draw on Wednesday night to extend their unbeaten streak to eight.
Jasinski entered in the 59th minute before scoring unassisted in the fifth minute of stoppage time for his second goal in his first 16 MLS appearances.

Defender Luc de Fougerolles used assists from defender Juan Manuel Sanabria and 19-year-old Aiden Hezarkhani to score his first goal in his second MLS appearance and give Real Salt Lake a 1-0 lead in the 79th minute. It was the eighth assist for Sanabria in his first season and the second for Hezarkhani in his 26th career appearance.
Angus Gunn totaled six saves in his 12th career start for fourth-place San Jose (13-8-8), which needed a win and some help to clinch a playoff spot in the Western Conference.
Rafael Cabral finished with one save for Real Salt Lake (9-14-6), which began the day in 11th place in the West.
San Jose improves to 7-4-5 on the road and has gone 4-0-4 during its unbeaten run.
Real Salt Lake has gone 1-5-2 since the start of September but is 9-4-3 overall at home.
San Jose entered with the second most road points this season at 25 — two less than Inter Miami.
San Jose: Hosts Nashville SC on Saturday.
Salt Lake: At Sporting Kansas City on Saturday.

title: Campbell hits 3 FGs as Western Kentucky defeats Sam Houston 16-3
summary: Brock Glenn and Coleson Arends connected on the game’s lone touchdown, Karl Campbell hit all three of his field goal attempts, and Western Kentucky took down Sam Houston 16-3 on Wednesday night
story: Brock Glenn and Coleson Arends connected on the game’s lone touchdown, Karl Campbell hit all three of his field goal attempts, and Western Kentucky took down Sam Houston 16-3 on Wednesday night

HUNTSVILLE, Texas -- Brock Glenn and Coleson Arends connected on the game's lone touchdown, Karl Campbell hit all three of his field goal attempts, and Western Kentucky took down Sam Houston 16-3 on Wednesday night.
The Hilltoppers (3-4, 2-1 Conference USA) remain perfect against Sam Houston since the Bearkats (1-5, 0-2) joined CUSA in 2023, and are 4-1 in the series.
Freshman Jonathan Stafford Jr. had five catches for 37 yards, and his 41 receptions are third on WKU's freshman receiving list.
WKU scored on its first possession of the game after forcing a Sam Houston three-and-out in just 50 seconds of game time.
Arends reeled in a 23-yard pass from Glenn to cap an 11-play, 65-yard drive.
Campbell connected on field goals of 33, 35, and 39 yards.
The Bearkats' only points came from Sam Carpenter's 42-yard field goal in the second quarter. They were held to 177 total yards, and managed just 12 first downs.
Freshman Westen Ard had a career-high 10 total tackles and 1 1/2 sacks.
Western Kentucky: host Delaware on Oct. 27.
Sam Houston: host New Mexico State on Oct. 21. ___

title: Roope Hintz scores in 4th round of shootout as Stars outlast Avalanche 3-2
summary: Roope Hintz scored in the fourth round of the shootout and the Dallas Stars beat Colorado 3-2 on Wednesday night in a game where the Avalanche had two early goals disallowed
story: Roope Hintz scored in the fourth round of the shootout and the Dallas Stars beat Colorado 3-2 on Wednesday night in a game where the Avalanche had two early goals disallowed
DENVER -- Roope Hintz scored in the fourth round of the shootout and the Dallas Stars beat Colorado 3-2 on Wednesday night in a game where the Avalanche had two early goals disallowed.
Hintz sent a wrist shot past Scott Wedgewood. Casey DeSmith secured the win by stopping Brock Nelson.
Miro Heiskanen and Arttu Hyry scored for the Stars, who split a back-to back set of games with the Avalanche. They lost 3-2 at home the night before.

Hyry nearly won it in overtime but sent a bouncing puck off the post. Hyry’s short-handed tally off a steal against Cale Makar gave the Stars a 2-1 lead early in the third period before Nelson tied it with 11:39 left.
Gabriel Landeskog also had a goal for Colorado.

The Avalanche had quite a night of disallowed goals and close calls. Jaden Schwartz saw his score overturned in the first period after the Stars successfully challenged for offsides. Later in the period, Gabriel Landeskog's goal was taken off the board when it was ruled the captain made a kicking motion to knock in the puck.

In the third, Gavin Brindley thought he scored and even began celebrating with teammates. But the officials never ruled it a goal and replays showed it glanced off both posts and didn't go into the net.
DeSmith finished with 25 saves for Dallas. He stopped three of four in the shootout. Stars forward Oskar Back suffered an upper-body injury in the first period and didn't return.
Makar returned to the lineup after missing Tuesday's game against the Stars. He and his wife welcomed twin boys on Wednesday morning.
Stars: At Chicago on Saturday.
Avalanche: Host Sidney Crosby and the Pittsburgh Penguins on Friday.

title: Brewers stun Dodgers with back-to-back homers in 7th inning and take 3-0 lead in NLCS with 6-2 win
summary: Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back homers off Blake Snell in the seventh inning to help the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-2 in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series
story: Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back homers off Blake Snell in the seventh inning to help the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-2 in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series
LOS ANGELES -- The Milwaukee Brewers hit the second-fewest home runs in baseball during the regular season, even as they topped the majors with 103 wins.
Maybe they were saving their biggest swings for the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell launched back-to-back homers off Blake Snell as Milwaukee regained the lead in the seventh inning, and the Brewers beat the Dodgers 6-2 on Wednesday to build a 3-0 cushion in the National League Championship Series.

Jackson Chourio also went deep on the first pitch of the game to help the Brewers close within one win of their first NL pennant. Milwaukee was in the American League when the franchise reached its only World Series, a seven-game loss to the St. Louis Cardinals in 1982.
“Job’s not finished yet,” Mitchell said.
Game 4 is Thursday at Dodger Stadium, where the Brewers can become the first major league club to complete a postseason sweep after getting swept by that same opponent in the previous postseason.
Los Angeles took all four games against Milwaukee in the NLCS last year.
The Dodgers had just gone ahead 2-1 in the sixth before getting stunned. The loss pushed the two-time defending World Series champions to the brink of elimination.
“All three games we’ve played so far, and hopefully that continues, where just every time they score, we come back and score,” Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. “That’s not easy to do in baseball.”
It was the fifth comeback victory in seven games this postseason for the Brewers, who have never beaten Los Angeles in three previous playoff series.
The only other time the Dodgers trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series, they were swept by the Baltimore Orioles in the 1966 World Series.
The lone team in big league history to come back from a 3-0 deficit to win a best-of-seven postseason series was the Boston Red Sox in the 2004 AL Championship Series against the New York Yankees.
“We’ve won four in a row a number of times this year,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “We've got to win tomorrow. That’s our only focus.”

Coming into the seventh, Snell had retired 14 batters in a row. The first pitch of the game thrown by the two-time Cy Young Award winner was hit for a home run by Chourio, and his last pitch was Mitchell's solo shot.

Andrew Vaughn drew a seven-pitch walk to open the inning and was replaced by pinch-runner Christian Yelich. Bauers followed with a 412-foot drive to right field on the 11th pitch of the at-bat for a 3-2 lead as most of the players in Milwaukee's dugout came onto the field to celebrate.
“I was looking for a fastball, and I didn’t want to miss it,” said Bauers, who had a team-leading 26 of Milwaukee's 154 regular-season homers.
It was his latest relentless plate appearance, too, after Bauers drew a 12-pitch walk from Yoshinobu Yamamoto that helped the Brewers go ahead early in Game 2.
“I think what changed for me this year was I stopped caring about results,” Bauers said. “I started caring about competing. I started caring about being in the moment and getting out of my own way.”
Watching Bauers work over Snell was “super sick,” Mitchell said.
And then it was his turn.

Mitchell's drive traveled 428 feet to right-center. That chased Snell, who hadn't given up a home run in 46 1/3 innings this year entering the game. It was the first time in his career he served up back-to-back homers to left-handed hitters and only the second time he gave up multiple longballs to left-handed batters in one game.

Bauers and Mitchell became just the third pair of left-handed hitters with consecutive postseason home runs off the same left-handed pitcher. Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper did it for Philadelphia against Atlanta reliever Dylan Lee in a Wild Card Series this year, and Babe Ruth and Lou Gehrig connected for the New York Yankees off Bill Sherdel of the St. Louis Cardinals in the 1928 World Series.
Snell gave up four runs and four hits in six-plus innings. He struck out nine and walked two.

The Brewers extended their lead to 5-2 in the eighth on Justin Wrobleski's wild pitch that scored Brice Turang, who reached on an infield single and advanced to third on William Contreras' single. They added another run on Joey Ortiz's two-strike RBI single in the ninth.
The offensively starved Dodgers took a 2-1 lead on Will Smith's two-run double off reliever Abner Uribe in the sixth.

After rookie starter Robert Gasser pitched five shutout innings, Uribe entered and loaded the bases on walks to Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker and Shohei Ohtani. Smith, who was 1 for 25 in the playoffs, doubled off the left-center fence with one out for his first hit of the NLCS.
DL Hall took over from Uribe and stranded runners at second and third by striking out pinch-hitter Kiké Hernández and Tommy Edman.
Hall allowed one hit in 2 1/3 scoreless innings to improve to 3-0 in these playoffs. Trevor Megill got four outs for his second save of the series and fourth this postseason.
The Dodgers played from behind again after the 22-year-old Chourio connected for his third career leadoff homer in the postseason as fans were still heading to their seats.
After that, Mitchell walked and Cooper Pratt singled in the second before Snell retired 14 in a row — six on strikeouts — before getting hammered in the seventh.
The Dodgers had runners on base in all but three innings, but couldn't get enough across. They have yet to homer in the NLCS and are 3 for 32 with runners in scoring position this postseason.
Ohtani was 1 for 2 with a walk while hitting sixth in the order, the lowest he's batted since joining the Dodgers three years ago.

title: Obeid kicks 20-yard FG as time expires, Missouri State beats Kennesaw State 24-21
summary: Yousef Obeid kicked a 20-yard field goal as time expired, Henry Belin IV had a career-high 300 yards passing and threw two touchdown passes to Isaiah Myers, and Missouri State defeated Kennesaw State 24-21 on Wednesday night
story: Yousef Obeid kicked a 20-yard field goal as time expired, Henry Belin IV had a career-high 300 yards passing and threw two touchdown passes to Isaiah Myers, and Missouri State defeated Kennesaw State 24-21 on Wednesday night

SPRINGFIELD, Mo. -- Yousef Obeid kicked a 20-yard field goal as time expired, Henry Belin IV had a career-high 300 yards passing and threw two touchdown passes to Isaiah Myers, and Missouri State defeated Kennesaw State 24-21 on Wednesday night.
The win was the first Bowl Subdivision victory for the Bears (2-4, 1-1 Conference USA) in the Casey Woods era. They previously defeated Championship Subdivision member Lindenwood on Sept. 12.
Myers had seven catches for 135 yards, twice tying the game in the second half with scoring grabs of 14 and 12 yards. Belin was 28-of-39 passing, and eight different receivers had catches.
The Bears held a 6-0 lead late in the second quarter thanks to two field goals from Obeid, but Kennesaw State took the lead into halftime with a 10-yard pass from Rickie Collins to Dylan Gary.

The teams traded scores in the second half until Missouri State took over possession with 6:06 remaining in regulation. They marched down the field with a 12-yard, 68-yard drive to set up Obeid's go-ahead field goal.

The Owls (1-5, 0-2) were paced by Collins's 260 yards passing on 27-of-35 passing, and Gary had 10 receptions for 135 yards. Kennesaw State has lost five straight since a 47-0 win over West Georgia in the season opener.
Kennesaw State: host Liberty on Oct. 22.
Missouri State: at Delaware on Oct. 20. ___

title: Kaick Ferreira, Daniel De Sousa Brito help Dallas end Sounders' unbeaten run with 1-0 victory
summary: Kaick Ferreira scored in the second half and Daniel De Sousa Britto made it stand up as FC Dallas beat Seattle 1-0 on Wednesday night, ending the Sounders’ four-match win streak and an unbeaten run that reached nine
story: Kaick Ferreira scored in the second half and Daniel De Sousa Britto made it stand up as FC Dallas beat Seattle 1-0 on Wednesday night, ending the Sounders’ four-match win streak and an unbeaten run that reached nine

FRISCO, Texas -- Kaick Ferreira scored in the second half and Daniel De Sousa Britto made it stand up as FC Dallas beat Seattle 1-0 on Wednesday night, ending the Sounders' four-match win streak and an unbeaten run that reached nine.

Ferreira took a pass from defender Osaze Urhoghide in the 63rd minute and scored for the fourth time this season after scoring twice in 27 appearances as a 19-year-old rookie last year. Urhoghide's helper was his third after collecting one last season in 27 matches as a rookie.
De Sousa Britto finished with seven saves for his third clean sheet in six starts with Dallas (14-7-8). He had 14 shutouts in 78 career starts with the San Jose Earthquakes before joining the club.
Andrew Thomas totaled two saves for Seattle (11-10-8), which went 4-0-5 during its unbeaten streak.

title: Union top Fire 3-1 for 8th straight victory during club-record 14-match unbeaten streak
summary: Bruno Damiani netted two goals after Milan Iloski scored — all with a man advantage — and Cavan Sullivan set a teen record for goal contributions as the Philadelphia Union beat the Chicago Fire 3-1 for their eighth straight victory in a club-record 14-...
story: Bruno Damiani netted two goals after Milan Iloski scored — all with a man advantage — and Cavan Sullivan set a teen record for goal contributions as the Philadelphia Union beat the Chicago Fire 3-1 for their eighth straight victory in a club-record 14-...

CHICAGO -- Bruno Damiani netted two goals after Milan Iloski scored — all with a man advantage — and Cavan Sullivan set a record for teenagers as the Philadelphia Union beat the Chicago Fire 3-1 on Wednesday night for their eighth straight victory in a club-record 14-match unbeaten streak.
Sullivan, who turned 17 this season, picked up his 14th assist on Damiani's first goal to set a league record for teens with 21 goal contributions this season.

Philadelphia (13-10-6) has gone 12-0-2 under interim coach Ryan Richter after he replaced Bradley Carnell at the end of May during the World Cup break. The Union started the day in sixth place after sitting last in the Eastern Conference before the coaching change.

Maren Haile-Selassie staked Chicago (14-9-6) to a 1-0 halftime lead with a goal in the 44th minute, but defender Jack Elliott was tagged with a yellow card in the 41st minute and again in the first minute of stoppage time, leaving the Fire a man down from there with his red-card exit.
Noah Allen and Jonathan Bamba had assists on Haile-Selassie's 11th goal of the campaign.
Iloski found the net four minutes into the second half to tie it 1-1. It was his sixth goal in the last four matches and his 18th of the season.
Damiani added the go-ahead score in the 55th minute and an insurance goal in the 67th, giving the striker 11 netters this season.
Damiani and defender Frankie Westfield had assists on Iloski's equalizer. Iloski joined Sullivan with an assist on Damiani's first netter and Jovan Lukic snagged one on his second goal.
Andre Blake stopped three shots on goal for Philadelphia.
Chris Brady finished with four saves for Chicago, which saw a three-match win streak end.
The Fire beat the Union 2-1 on the road to close out March.
Chicago falls to 9-5-1 at home, while Philadelphia improves to 5-7-2 on the road.
The Union haven't lost since a 6-4 setback on the road at Inter Miami on May 24.

story: Hany Mukhtar and Andy Nájar each had a goal and an assist, Sam Surridge also scored a goal and Nashville SC beat Sporting Kansas City 3-0 for their fourth consecutive win

Roughly halfway through the first, Montreal regained the lead, as Hutson, playing against younger brother Cole for the first time, beat Charlie Lindgren on a quick shot from the slot. Wednesday's victory came after Miami routed DC United 4-0 last Saturday on a pair of goals from Messi and Suárez, and it was the second league win for new coach Cristian “Kily” González, who took over Sept. 16.

Berterame scored in the 20th for his eighth goal of the season. De Paul doubled Miami's lead right before the end of the first half. Dayne St. Clair denied Nicolás Fernández on a penalty in the final minute of the match for his second straight clean sheet.

It has been a rollercoaster year for Messi, who led Argentina to its second straight World Cup final and announced his retirement from international soccer a month later. Now, he has a chance to cap it with another trophy.

title: Shohei Ohtani at No. 6, a lone single, and the Dodgers staring at elimination
summary: Shohei Ohtani singled after being dropped to sixth in the order for the Los Angeles Dodgers
story: Shohei Ohtani singled after being dropped to sixth in the order for the Los Angeles Dodgers

LOS ANGELES -- Slumping Shohei Ohtani singled after being dropped to sixth in the order for the Los Angeles Dodgers, whose 6-2 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series put them on the brink of postseason elimination on Wednesday night.

It's the lowest the left-handed hitting Ohtani has hit since joining the Dodgers three years ago on a $700 million, 10-year contract. Manager Dave Roberts wanted to alternate right- and left-handed hitters throughout the lineup against Milwaukee's left-handed starter Robert Gasser.
”Shohei’s all on board," Roberts said before the game. “Whatever it takes to win.”
It wasn't enough, and now the two-time defending World Series champions trail 3-0 in the best-of-seven series.
Ohtani flied out in the second, got hit by a pitch in the fourth and walked in the sixth before singling with two outs in the eighth. The Dodgers had runners on base in all but three innings.
“We’re just not getting those timely hits,” Roberts said afterward. “We’ve had some opportunities with guys on base, but can’t get that hit.”

Ohtani, the designated hitter, is typically atop the order, but Roberts has dropped him lower during a slump that has extended into the postseason. Ohtani has been struggling with left knee and right biceps issues for a few months, and said before the National League Division Series that he's not 100% healthy.
During his six years with the Los Angeles Angels, Ohtani started games batting sixth or lower 19 times, all during the 2020 season or earlier.
Ohtani is hitting .182 (4 for 22) over seven postseason games. He has seven strikeouts, four walks and one stolen base with no home runs, no RBIs and an OPS of .533.
He hasn’t homered since Aug. 18 at Colorado.

“I couldn’t imagine really kind of having the expectations that he has and falling short in a way that it’s not normal for him,” teammate Mookie Betts said before the game. “Then having to come back and be present in this postseason knowing how important he is to the boys.”
Roberts said he saw a more focused Ohtani during off-day batting practice Tuesday.

“He was determined, and that’s an understatement,” the manager said. “He was here late last night working on his swing, out with the guys and talking about things on how we're going to beat these guys.”
Dodgers pitcher Tyler Glasnow, set to start Game 4 on Thursday, said Ohtani's demeanor doesn't deviate regardless of how well he's performing.

“I think most people put in that situation, you’d have a lot more emotional volatility, so it’s just impressive to see him just be a good dude always,” Glasnow said. “I don’t think he needs reassurance or anything. He’s confident in himself. It’s just business as usual and a lot of smiles and the same laugh.”

title: A wall of screens, 32 teams and 1 mission: How NHL Player Safety tracks trouble in real time
summary: The NHL's Player Safety room in Manhattan is buzzing with activity, especially on busy nights when all 32 teams are in action
story: The NHL's Player Safety room in Manhattan is buzzing with activity, especially on busy nights when all 32 teams are in action
NEW YORK -- The puck dropped just after 6 p.m. in Detroit, and the hum of activity had long been underway inside the NHL Player Safety room at league headquarters in Manhattan.

Someone was assigned to every game, and this was the busiest night of the season so far with all 32 teams in action. The room is a hockey lover's paradise with five giant television screens and more than a dozen other monitors showing every single goal, save, hit, penalty, injury and more.
The watchers who work there like to say they see everything. And they have an important job to do.

This is the first line of defense for head injuries, with a vast majority of the communication coming as calls to concussion spotters monitoring for the need to pull players off the ice for evaluation. It is also the beginning of the process to determine supplemental discipline, with an intricate process of watching, vetting, logging and reporting questionable plays to determine potential suspensions and fines long before George Parros hands them down and video explanations come out.
General managers, coaches and players are welcome to visit. The department was established in 2011.

“For the most part, when people come in, they do leave with knowing at least one thing: We definitely saw what you think that we should see,” said Damian Echevarrieta, the NHL's senior vice president of player safety. “Now, you might not always agree with our decisions, but the fact that we are on top of it and notice every single incident of every game, I think people really leave here knowing that.”
The Associated Press sat in Tuesday night to see how it all goes down.

With 16 games going as part of ESPN's “Frozen Frenzy,” there are concussion spotters seated at the front of the control room. It is the responsibility of, on this night, eight game-watchers to first alert a spotter of any possible contact to the head. Spotters then have a direct line to reach team medical staffs at games.

The first call comes at 6:33 p.m. to look at New Jersey's Jack Hughes high-sticking Detroit's Keegan Kolesar. It's quickly cleared of being a spotter concern, but Echevarrieta wants the video clipped just in case for later.
Just after 7 p.m., spotters are made aware of Florida's Lars Eller taking a puck to the face in the first period at Columbus and leaving the ice to get stitched up.

Later, it's Montreal's Noah Dobson, and there is chatter throughout the night as they keep an eye on him for any visible signs of a concussion. Game-watchers have access to Hawk-Eye camera angles from each end of the ice, along with a full-rink view from high above and the ability to isolate on a single player.
Another task is making sure all players required to wear helmets in warmups are doing so, along with mandatory neck guards for first-year players.

Anyone doing a rookie lap, like Anaheim's Roger McQueen on Tuesday night, gets a grace period — but when he was still helmetless several minutes later, Player Safety was ready to call the arena. McQueen had his helmet on two minutes later.

At 7:52 p.m., Panthers defenseman Uvis Balinskis was down on the ice and replays show Blue Jackets forward Mathieu Olivier spearing his opponent in the groin. Echevarrieta and Co. clock it before officials review the video and eject Olivier with a game misconduct for slashing.

Any time there is the potential for further punishment, a report catalogs what happened, if there was a penalty called, the players involved, any disciplinary history, the aggressor's next game and video clips of the incident. That report is sent to the entire department.

When Parros, a retired enforcer who took over player safety decisions in 2017, deems something worthy of a possible review, he emails Echevarrieta and the rest of the room for thoughts to be shared just with him. Parros asked by 8:17 p.m., less than a half-hour after the play unfolded.
On Wednesday, Olivier was fined $5,000, the maximum allowed under the collective bargaining agreement. A suspension was determined not to be warranted in part because he had no disciplinary history.

Seattle goaltender Philipp Grubauer shoving Philadelphia's Trevor Zegras raised attention around the room not long after. That was more to have video evidence of a goalie roughing penalty for future reference.

Echevarrieta has been with the NHL since 1999, working in hockey operations in Toronto under Colin Campbell. That is still where the situation room does the same daily monitoring — but for goal reviews to determine if the puck is over the goal line and to assist with coach's challenges.
A decade and a half ago came the opportunity to copy many of the same procedures to use in Player Safety.
“It was already a time-tested system that we put into place, and it’s worked really well,” Echevarrieta said.

Repetition over the years has helped, he said, to where now even the most chaotic nights like Tuesday run smoothly. Interspersed in the job responsibilities is plenty of hockey talk — Matthew Tkachuk assisting on brother Brady's natural hat trick, and the few-seconds spoiler — “(Alexis) Lafrenière scored again!”

At multiple points, 10 games were going on at the same time, with Echevarrieta switching the sound to the most important broadcast at the moment and overseeing action that included 136 penalties, 110 goals and five fights — including the second of the young season for Colorado's Nathan MacKinnon. Overheard was the amazed sentiment, "“Nate fought again?”
And he wants anyone working in hockey to see how the sausage is made, a five-minute walk from where the Rangers play their home games at Madison Square Garden.
“MSG’s right down the street,” Echevarrieta said. “If you’re in town, especially if you have a day off in between an Islanders and a Rangers game, the door’s always open.”

title: Seahawks and Broncos dealing with top defenses and shaky QB play as they kick off Week 6
summary: The Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos kick off Week 6 on Thursday night
story: The Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos kick off Week 6 on Thursday night
DENVER -- Two dominant defenses doing all the heavy lifting. Two struggling quarterbacks trying everything to recapture last year's magic.

The Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos kick off Week 6 on Thursday night in the cold at Empower Field with both teams trying to avoid a third loss, which would match last year's total for a full season.

These teams appeared headed toward a Super Bowl collision eight months ago before Bo Nix broke his right ankle in the playoffs and Jarrett Stidham cratered in a 10-7 loss to New England in the AFC championship.

Seattle manhandled the Patriots in the Super Bowl for the franchise's second championship, but the MVP of that game, Kenneth Walker III, left for Kansas City in free agency and the Seahawks haven't been the same.
Sam Darnold has thrown five interceptions in three games this season, including two Sunday that the San Francisco 49ers turned into quick touchdowns on their way to a win in Seattle.
“Just got to continue to trust myself, trust my feet, trust what I’m seeing, which I’m doing. But, yeah, just got to be better taking care of the football,” Darnold said.

Nix has regressed this season. His recent comments paint a picture of a gun-shy quarterback hesitant to throw the ball downfield. Although his protection has been spotty at times, he keeps bailing on clean pockets and is reluctant to tuck the ball and run it himself, negating his dual-threat traits.
When talking about his uneven play, Nix goes back and forth between offering assurances of improvement and denying there's any problem at all.

“Playing good and playing bad, it’s a narrative and I think it’s honestly kind of something we make up,” Nix said. “I don’t think necessarily I’m playing any different than what I’m normally playing.”
Stats say otherwise.
His passer rating, completion percentage and yards per pass attempt are all down from last year and he threw for just 123 yards in Denver's 23-17 road win over the Los Angeles Chargers last weekend.

“He gets a lot of flak for just being the starting quarterback,’’ Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton said. “We all have certain things that come with our job description and for him, he has a lot of weight on his shoulder. … Everyone has his back. We all know that for us to have success, we need him to be able to have that success. And we’re going to always have his back, no matter what, good, bad or indifferent.”
Seattle (3-2) at Denver (3-2).
When/where to watch: Thursday, 8:15 p.m. EDT, Prime Video.
Latest odds: Seahawks by 1 1/2.
Against the spread: Seattle 1-2-2, Denver 3-2.
Last week: Seahawks lost to San Francisco 49ers 32-29; Broncos beat Chargers 23-17.
Last meeting: Seahawks beat Broncos 26-20 on Sept. 8, 2024, at Lumen Field in Seattle.
Series record: Broncos lead, 35-23.

Nix vs. a Seahawks defense that is ranked first in the NFL in yards per play, interceptions and takeaways and net yards and passing yards per game. Broncos coach Sean Payton is calling the plays again after he demoted OC Davis Webb a week ago, but Nix has still been in his own head a lot no matter who's in his ear. Payton, on whether resuming the play calling was akin to getting back on a bike: “I wish it was like riding a bike because my memories of riding bikes were always carefree, relaxing,” he said with a laugh.
— Broncos pass-rusher Nik Bonitto leads the league with seven multi-sack games since the start of last season.
— The Broncos have recorded multiple sacks in 19 consecutive home games. That's the longest such streak in team history and the longest current streak in the NFL.

— Since the start of 2024, the Seahawks have the highest road winning percentage (.842, 16-3) in the NFL and the Broncos have the second-highest home winning percentage, also at .842 with a 16-3 record.
— Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba leads the NFL with 583 receiving yards and seven TD catches.

— Nix has 13 career game-winning drives in the fourth quarter or overtime, tied with Justin Herbert and Matt Ryan for the second-most by a player in his first three seasons since 1970. Only Dak Prescott (14) had more.
With contributions from AP Sports Writer Anne M. Peterson.

title: Shai Hope’s 102 gives West Indies series-leveling win over India in fourth cricket T20
summary: Shai Hope has set a West Indies record by reaching 102 not out as West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth cricket T20 to level the five-match series at 2-2
story: Shai Hope has set a West Indies record by reaching 102 not out as West Indies beat India by 24 runs in the fourth cricket T20 to level the five-match series at 2-2
HYDERABAD, India -- Shai Hope set a West Indies record by reaching 102 not out as West Indies beat India by 24 runs Wednesday in the fourth cricket T20 to level the five-match series at 2-2.
Hope hit nine sixes and four fours in his third T20 century – the most for a West Indies batter – as the visitors piled up 247-3 in 20 overs. India had won the toss and opted to bowl.
It was the second-highest first innings total in T20s against India, trailing England’s 257-3 in Southampton this year.
In reply, Sanju Samson hit 56 off 23 balls but India was down to 130-5 and the chase never took off. It finished with 223 in 19.3 overs.
Keemo Paul picked 5-41 for his second five-wicket haul in T20s.
Bengaluru will host the deciding T20 on Saturday.
Put into bat, Hope gave West Indies a flying by putting on 52 off 26 balls with Jewel Andrew (21). Axar Patel trapped Andrew lbw in the fifth over but West Indies still got 79-1 in the powerplay.
Hope then added another 58 off 24 balls with Shimron Hetmyer, reaching 50 off 28 balls with the help of five sixes. He sped to a second hundred in the series with another four sixes.
Hope also became only the fifth batter to score multiple hundreds in a bilateral T20 series. Overall, it was his fourth hundred in seven innings across ODIs and T20s on this tour.
He wasn’t finished, despite Prince Yadav sending back Hetmyer for 33, while Rovman Powell scored 24.
Sherfane Rutherford scored 49 not out off 26 balls to provide the final flourish, hitting four fours and three sixes, as West Indies breached 200.

Hope and Rutherford added 91 off only 43 balls, as India served a slow over-rate penalty in the final over. Nitish Reddy gave away 19 runs in the 20th, with Hope reaching his century with a six off the last ball.
In reply, Samson hit four sixes to give India a quick start. He and Abhishek Sharma (29) added 60 off 25 balls as India scored 80-2 in the powerplay.
Keemo Paul struck twice in the fifth over – Samson was out caught at square leg on the first ball and then three balls later, Ishan Kishan was caught at deep mid wicket for six.
India also lost skipper Shreyas Iyer (16) before the halfway mark, and was down to 97-3.
Abhishek Sharma didn’t get going, scoring 29 off 24 balls, with three fours and a six. His dismissal was the turning point – he was caught off Gudakesh Motie at long off in the 12th over.
Motie also had Naman Dhir stumped for a golden duck.
Tilak Varma fought hard with 43 off 25 balls along with Nitish Reddy’s cameo (41 off 20 balls) but it went in vain.
Paul picked three wickets in the 19th over to wrap up the innings.
